**NASA FIRE INTELLIGENCE – Flame in Free Fall**

NASA FIRE INTELLIGENCE is a proposed intelligent platform designed to organize and analyze scientific research on fire behavior in microgravity. It addresses the challenge of scattered scientific information by collecting, classifying, and processing NASA combustion experiment data. The platform will use artificial intelligence and statistical methods to summarize research, compare experiments, identify patterns, analyze relationships between variables, and detect potential fire risks. Its interactive dashboard will present findings and evidence-based recommendations in an accessible way. This project is important because fire behaves differently in space, creating unique safety challenges for astronauts, spacecraft, and space habitats. By making scientific information easier to access and understand, our solution aims to support fire prevention, improve risk assessment, and contribute to safer future missions to the Moon and Mars.

Project Details – NASA FIRE INTELLIGENCE: Flame in Free Fall

NASA FIRE INTELLIGENCE is a proposed platform designed to transform scientific data about combustion in microgravity into useful information for astronaut safety.

How it works: The system follows five main stages: data collection from NASA research and combustion experiments, organization according to variables such as fuel, temperature, oxygen concentration, and airflow, data processing and standardization, intelligent analysis using artificial intelligence and statistical methods, and visualization through an interactive dashboard.

The AI component is intended to summarize scientific research, identify similarities between experiments, detect relationships between variables, classify combustion conditions, identify potential risk scenarios, and generate evidence-based explanations and recommendations.

Benefits and expected impact: The platform aims to reduce the time needed to find scientific information, make experiment comparisons easier, improve understanding of fire behavior in microgravity, and support safer decisions when selecting materials and designing spacecraft and space habitats. Its expected impact includes supporting fire prevention research and improving astronaut safety during future missions to the Moon, Mars, and space stations.

Tools and technologies: The proposal identifies artificial intelligence, statistical analysis, scientific databases, data-processing methods, and an interactive dashboard as key components. Specific programming languages, hardware, and software platforms have not yet been defined in the project document.

Creativity and team considerations: The creative aspect is the integration of scattered scientific research into one intelligent platform that can interpret, compare, and present information in an accessible way. Our team considered data reliability, experiment conditions, scientific evidence, usability, fire risks in enclosed environments, and the safety needs of astronauts. We also plan to validate the results and document the source of the information used.
